statement:
Given a non-negative real \(a\) and a sequence \((u_n)\) defined by \(u_1 = 3\) and \(u_{n+1} = \dfrac{u_n}{2} + \dfrac{n^2}{4n^2+a}\sqrt{u_n^2+3}\).
a) For \(a = 0\), prove that the sequence is convergent and find its limit.
b) For \(a \in [0,1]\), prove that the sequence is convergent.

If \(a, b, c\) are nonnegative real numbers, prove that
\[3(a^2+b^2+c^2) \geq (a+b+c)(\sqrt{ab}+\sqrt{bc}+\sqrt{ca}) + (a-b)^2+(b-c)^2+(c-a)^2 \geq (a+b+c)^2.\]

Given circumcircle \((O)\) with fixed points \(B, C\) (\(BC\) not a diameter). Point \(A\) varies on \((O)\) so that \(\triangle ABC\) is acute. Let \(E, F\) be the feet of the altitudes from \(B, C\). Let \((I)\) be a variable circle through \(E\) and \(F\).
a) Assume \((I)\) is tangent to \(BC\) at \(D\). Prove that \(\dfrac{DB}{DC} = \sqrt{\dfrac{\cot B}{\cot C}}\).
b) Assume \((I)\) meets \(BC\) at \(M\) and \(N\). Let \(H\) be the orthocenter and \(P, Q\) the intersections of \((I)\) and the circumcircle of \(\triangle HBC\). The circumcircle \((K)\) through \(P, Q\) tangent to \((O)\) at \(T\) (on the same side as \(A\) with respect to \(PQ\)). Prove that the interior angle bisector of \(\angle MTN\) passes through a fixed point.

Let \(\{f_n(x)\}\) be a sequence of polynomials with \(f_0(x) = 2\), \(f_1(x) = 3x\), and
\[f_n(x) = 3xf_{n-1}(x) + (1 - x - 2x^2)f_{n-2}(x)  (n \geq 2).\]
Determine all values of \(n\) such that \(f_n(x)\) is divisible by \(x^3 - x^2 + x\).

For \(a, n \in \mathbb{Z}^+\), consider the equation \(a^2 x + 6ay + 36z = n\) where \(x, y, z \in \mathbb{N}\).
a) Find all \(a\) such that for all \(n \geq 250\), the equation always has non-negative integer solutions.
b) Given \(a > 1\) and \(\gcd(a,6) = 1\), find the greatest value of \(n\) (in terms of \(a\)) for which the equation has no non-negative integer solution.

There are \(m\) boys and \(n\) girls (\(m, n \geq 2\)) in a duet singing contest. Each show consists of some boy-girl duets where each pair sings at most once and each participant sings at least once. Two shows are different if some pair sings in one but not the other. The contest ends when every possible show has been performed exactly once.
a) A show is called \emph{dependent} on participant \(X\) if removing all of \(X\)'s duets leaves at least one other participant with no songs. Prove that among all shows dependent on \(X\), the number with an odd total of songs equals the number with an even total.
b) Prove that the organizers can order the shows so that the number of songs in any two consecutive shows have different parity.
